thread:
erin: Quick heads-up — while triaging a 502 cascade I found a Postgres error log in prod that includes a JSON blob with a field named "client_secret". Not sure if it's fully present or partially masked. Can someone do a quick privacy scope? pinging @miguel @lia

miguel: can you paste a redacted snippet? don't post real secrets, just surrounding keys/lengths or masked string so we can assess exposure

erin: here's the exact log line I pulled (redacted partial secret):
```
ERROR query-runner: 2026-03-17T18:23:10Z rpc=12345 payload={"user_id":12345,"client_id":"abc_789","client_secret":"sk_live_4c1e6f2b9d3a...","query":"INSERT INTO ..."} stack=...
```

lia: that looks like a ~30 char secret fragment present, which likely means a live secret. Where are these logs coming from? pod name / logging pipeline?

erin: from the `query-runner` deployment. logs go to stdout -> fluentd -> prod-logs index. I ran `kubectl -n prod logs deploy/query-runner | grep client_secret` to find it.

taylor: incidents-bot please create an incident if we need rotations and comms

incidents-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — INC-2026-3177 by erin. Severity: P2. Channels: #incidents, #eng-security.

miguel: Security ops: if that's a full secret we should rotate immediately and treat as potential exposure. First check: are these customer OAuth tokens or internal service creds? Pattern looks like oauth access tokens (client_secret) — leaning toward customer/integration secrets.

lia: the code path shows it's logging the whole oauth response on error. That implies incoming third-party client secrets may be logged. We need to assume customer-impact until proven otherwise. Recommend: 1) restrict index ACLs now, 2) rotate affected keys, 3) forensic who queried those logs.

erin: I've tightened ACL on the prod-logs index to SRE+eng-security only. pls don't search across the index broadly. Example query I used: `curl -s "https://logs.internal/prod/_search?q=client_secret"` — do not run ad-hoc.

jason: Security lead here. Agreed with Lia. Action list: scope affected customer ids, rotate secrets, enforce redaction, and prepare comms. Need legal sign-off before external notifications — tagging @kate.

kate: Legal: we'll need a short timeline and list of affected customers. No external comms until we confirm whether secrets were complete/full and whether any access happened. If there's a 30+ char prefix we must treat as live unless we can verify truncation at proxy.

miguel: I'll start rotating keys matching the pattern and will run a search for related tokens. Will also open a PR to redact `client_secret` at the logging callsite. PR: https://git.internal/r/query-runner/merge_requests/123 (masking before logging).

taylor: I'll review the PR and add a fluentd filter to drop fields named `client_secret` at ingestion. Small config change can block future occurrences.

jason: For now, prepare an internal advisory for Sales/Support with a short FAQ. Legal to review external wording once we know impacted customers and rotation plan. @kate to own external approval.

kate: I'll draft templates and hold them pending the impact list + rotation plan. Also need to know if rotation will break customer integrations so Support can pre-emptively triage.

incidents-bot: Assigned INC-2026-3177 -> eng-sre, eng-security.

erin: Action items (summary):
- miguel: rotate suspected keys and post rotated IDs here
- lia + jason: run access audit (who viewed the log entries in last 7 days)
- taylor: review and merge redaction PR + add fluentd rule
- kate: draft comms templates, hold for approval

miguel: starting rotation now, ETA ~40m. will post results and list of rotated client_ids (no secrets).

lia: running access audit query, will share results in 15m.

erin: thanks everyone. keep updates in this thread only. If you need to escalate to execs, ping jason directly. :thumbsup:
